overall: Board did not violate the law on the April 14 notice, which reasonably withheld litigation details to protect its position. It did violate the law on the April 28 notice, which omitted the police unions named in the executive session; a post-complaint amendment did not cure it.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the April 14 notice gave too vague an executive session purpose, listing only litigation strategy without naming the litigation matters.
allegations.key_passage: Because including this information could have had a detrimental effect on the Board's litigating position, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting certain information regarding the anticipated executive session on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the April 28 notice listed only 'Negotiations Update' for executive session, without naming the police unions being negotiated with.
allegations.key_passage: Amending meeting notices after the fact does not achieve the Open Meeting Law's purpose of notifying the public as to what topics a public body plans to discuss.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements.

The Board may not rely upon the Open Meeting Law as the basis for continuing to withhold the minutes of the April 28 executive session (attorney-client privilege or Public Records Law exemptions may still apply).
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
